text: Confirm the messages are actually being generated and reaching the journal at all: `logger -t invoiced 'probe'` then `journalctl -t invoiced --no-pager | tail`. They're right there. So the app and journald are both fine -- the problem is specifically between journald and whatever rsyslog is supposed to do with them.

`cat /etc/rsyslog.d/25-invoiced.conf` shows a completely correct, ordinary rule filing `invoiced`-tagged messages to `/var/log/invoiced/invoiced.log`. rsyslog itself is running (`systemctl status rsyslog`). So why would a correct rule never fire? Think about *how* messages even reach rsyslog on a systemd box in the first place -- check `systemctl status rsyslog` closely for what socket it acquired.

rsyslog picked up `/run/systemd/journal/syslog` -- that's the socket journald forwards traditional syslog-formatted copies of journal entries to. rsyslog isn't reading the journal directly; it only sees what journald chooses to forward there. Check journald's merged config: `systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/journald.conf` and look at `ForwardToSyslog=`.

It's set to `no` -- so nothing journald receives ever gets forwarded to rsyslog, no matter how correct rsyslog's own rules are. Fix the drop-in (`sudo sed -i 's/ForwardToSyslog=no/ForwardToSyslog=yes/' /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/noforward.conf`), then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`. Verify: `logger -t invoiced 'confirm'` then `tail /var/log/invoiced/invoiced.log`.
